metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.note: 3m: state 3 reasons thermocouple is suitable for measuring the temperature of the blue part of a candle flame. 3 slots × 1m each. Correct reasons: high temperature range / fast response time / small sensing junction / gives electrical output. Distractors: reasons correct for mercury-in-glass or clinical thermometer (large bulb, slow response, low range).

question.name: CSEC Phy Jun 2023 Q4a(ii) — Thermocouple Suitability for Candle Flame
question.text:
A thermocouple thermometer is used to measure the temperature of the blue part of the flame of a small candle.

State THREE reasons why a thermocouple thermometer is suitable for this application.

Reason 1: [[1]]

Reason 2: [[2]]

Reason 3: [[3]]
question.general_feedback:
Why the thermocouple is suitable for measuring the blue part of a candle flame:

  1. High temperature range — thermocouples can measure up to ~1500 °C or more; a candle flame reaches ~1400 °C. Mercury-in-glass thermometers max out at ~350 °C.
  2. Fast (rapid) response — the thermocouple junction responds almost instantly to temperature changes, capturing the correct temperature in a small, fluctuating flame.
  3. Small/fine sensing junction — the tiny wire junction fits within a specific, localised region of the flame (the blue zone), giving a point measurement rather than an average.
  4. Gives an electrical output — the EMF (voltage) can be read on a digital display or recorded by a data logger, allowing accurate readings without the observer needing to be close to the flame.

options.text: Small sensing junction — measures a localised region

groups.label: Reason 1 thermocouple suits candle flame measurement
groups.diagnostic_hint: The thermocouple has a HIGH TEMPERATURE RANGE (up to ~1500°C), making it suitable for a candle flame (~1400°C). A liquid-in-glass thermometer would vaporise.

options.text: Small sensing junction — measures a localised region

groups.label: Reason 2 thermocouple suits candle flame measurement
groups.diagnostic_hint: A thermocouple has a FAST RESPONSE — it responds almost instantly to temperature changes, important for measuring a fluctuating flame.

options.text: Small sensing junction — measures a localised region

groups.label: Reason 3 thermocouple suits candle flame measurement
groups.diagnostic_hint: The thermocouple junction is SMALL — it can be inserted into the localised region of the flame without significantly disturbing it.

word_bank: Small sensing junction — measures a localised region
ddwtos.word_bank_note: 7 tokens for 3 slots. 4 correct — any 3 earn full marks. 'Large bulb for good sensitivity' describes a mercury-in-glass thermometer and is irrelevant (a large bulb cannot fit in the blue zone of a candle flame). 'Slow response allows stable reading' is wrong — a slow response would miss the actual peak temperature of a fluctuating flame. 'Safe to use below 100°C only' is a limitation, not a suitability reason, and incorrectly describes a thermocouple (which operates well above 100°C).
